Anyone may call it. It buys $LORH with the ETH it holds and burns what it receives. One buy is small: a fixed share of the ETH in the market it buys on, sized so that the price it moves is less than a trade round it costs in fees. What was spent comes back as allowance over ten minutes. It keeps the last five prices it wrote down, a quarter of an hour apart at the least, sets the lowest aside and does not buy more than 5% above the next lowest. A price that was pushed up has to hold for most of an hour before it is bought at. It has no withdraw function. ETH can leave it only as a purchase of $LORH.

Holdavia is a market on Robinhood Chain for locked bags. A holder sells tokens below the pool price in exchange for a lock. The buyer pays ETH today and receives a position that unlocks on a set date. The position can itself be sold, so the tokens never reach the pool before the date.

The contract has no price feed. It knows one number: the ETH price the seller asked for. The discount shown in the app is a display, and it never changes what a buyer pays.

The holder sets an ETH price. The app shows the discount that price gives the next buyer for the time left on the lock. When a buyer pays, the position moves to them, the ETH goes to the seller, 1% is burned, and the unlock date does not change.
The launchpad's owner can re-point a coin's future creator fees after a public three-day delay. The market does not depend on that income.

The lens reads the market for the app, a whole screen in one call. The art contract draws each position's picture on the chain: the coin, the amount, the unlock date and a ring that shows how far the lock has run. Neither holds anything, and replacing either does not touch the market.
The market is complete without the token. Holding it changes when you can act, and every fill shrinks its supply.

The team's purchase is sold through the market as listing #1: 30% under the pool, locked 30 days. The ETH goes to the published operations wallet, and its first use is an external review of the market contract. After listing #1 fills, the team holds no $LORH.
The token adds optional access and a visible burn story. The market price still comes from each listing.
The tokens sit in escrow. The key moves. Whoever holds it when the clock reaches zero can claim the whole bag.
There is no treasury share of these fees and no address that can redirect them. The buyer pays the listed price and nothing on top. Claiming costs only the network fee.
Time is worth money, and a market can price it.
Time is worth money, and a market can price it. A seller who takes ETH today accepts a lower price. A buyer who can wait pays less.
Two contracts hold the money. Everything else only reads.

Two fills of one listing can unlock on different days. A position cannot be split and cannot be claimed before its date. There is no penalty exit. The way out before the date is to sell the position. After the unlock time anyone may trigger the release; the tokens can only go to the current holder.
